### Problem
With `MultiIndex` columns, `to_excel` wrote a NaN column label as the last value of that level (in the report, the NaN bin from `pd.cut` became `(0.0, inf]`).

### Cause
`_format_header_mi` calls `levels.take(level_codes)` without `allow_fill=True`, so the `-1` code of a NaN label wraps around to the last element. The row-index path already passes `allow_fill=True`.

### Fix
Pass `allow_fill=True`; the NaN is then written as `na_rep` (an empty cell), same as NaN row-index labels.

### Test
`test_to_excel_multiindex_nan_column_label` runs for all engines and `merge_cells` values and reads the header rows back with `header=None`, because `read_excel` with `header=[0, 1]` forward-fills empty header cells (which is why the test in #62576 passed on `main`). Fails on `main`, passes with this change.
title: BUG: to_excel wrote NaN MultiIndex column label as last level value (GH#62340)
